question: Lysozyme, which is present in egg, has ___________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**bacteriostatic property.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Egg white contains lysozyme**, an essential ingredient with antibacterial capabilities, particularly against Gram-positive bacteria.
 
• Research suggests that chemical or physical alterations may increase the** lysozyme's **range of activity.
 
• The goal of the study was to evaluate the **antibacterial activity of lysozyme-modified bacteria** against a number of different types of bacteria. 
 
• A material that can **prevent bacterial growth and reproduction** without necessarily** killing the organism is known as a bacteriostatic agent or medication.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Probiotic property **

 
 
• **​Probiotics are defined as living bacteria** that provide the host with health benefits when given in sufficient quantity.
 
• **Eli Metchnikoff**, the recipient of the Nobel Prize and often considered as the father of **contemporary probiotics**, is credited with making the first observations about the advantageous traits certain **bacteria bestow.**
 
 
 
• **Universal solubility property** 
 
 
• **​Water is referred to as a "universal solvent"** because it has a considerably wider range of natural solvent properties than any other liquid. Water, however, cannot always dissolve all compounds. For instance, because oppositely charged particles are not highly soluble in water, hydroxides, fats, or waxes cannot be dissolved by them.
 
 
 
• **Agonistic property ** 
 
 
• **An agonist** is a chemical that triggers a biological response by activating a **receptor**.** **The actions of other **cellular elements activate cellular proteins** referred to as **receptors.** In contrast, an **antagonist prevents the agonist's action from occurring**, while an inverse agonist produces the opposite effect.
